executive_summary.tagline: Empowering farmers market vendors with simple tools to manage sales and grow their business.
executive_summary.problem_statement: Farmers market vendors struggle with inefficient manual processes for inventory management, sales tracking, and payment reconciliation, leading to lost revenue, wasted time, and potential compliance issues.
executive_summary.solution_overview: MarketTable is a mobile point-of-sale (POS) application designed specifically for farmers market vendors. It offers features like inventory management, sales tracking, digital payment processing, and reporting, all in one easy-to-use platform.
executive_summary.value_proposition: MarketTable helps farmers market vendors save time, increase sales, and make better business decisions by providing a streamlined, affordable, and market-specific POS solution.
target_users: Small farmers market vendors with existing digital payment adoption (e.g., already using Square or PayPal).
Direct-to-consumer farms selling at on-site farm stands looking to streamline operations.
executive_summary.target_market_size: The TAM is estimated at $1B, based on the total number of farmers market vendors in the US and their average annual revenue. The SAM is $200M, representing vendors already using digital payment solutions. The SOM is $20M, targeting early adopters in select regions with strong local food movements.
key_differentiators: Market-specific features like offline mode and vendor-specific reporting.
Competitive transaction fees compared to general POS systems.
Simple and intuitive interface designed for non-technical users.
executive_summary.competitive_landscape: The market is dominated by general POS systems like Square and Shopify, which offer broader functionality but lack market-specific features. Local Line offers similar services but is focused on online sales and distribution, leaving a gap for a market-specific POS solution.
executive_summary.revenue_model: Tiered SaaS subscription (Free, Basic, Pro) and transaction fees on digital payments.
top_risks: Competition from existing POS systems: Mitigate by focusing on niche features and building strong relationships with farmers markets.
Technical debt due to rushed development: Mitigate by prioritizing code quality and investing in automated testing.
Low user adoption due to lack of awareness: Mitigate by implementing a targeted marketing strategy and offering incentives for early adopters.
executive_summary.regulatory_summary: Compliance with PCI DSS for payment processing and state data breach notification laws.
executive_summary.gtm_strategy: Direct sales at farmers markets, online advertising, and content marketing targeting small vendors in regions with strong local food movements.
key_milestones: Launch MVP in beachhead market (6 months)

key_decisions.recommendation: Defer decision until pricing sensitivity is validated through EXP-2. A/B test different pricing models in the beachhead market.

job_to_be_done.success_definition: Having accurate sales records, minimizing wasted inventory, and receiving payments promptly and reliably, while spending minimal time on administrative tasks.

current_behaviour.why_problem_persists: Cost of sophisticated POS systems is prohibitive for small vendors. Existing solutions are often fragmented and require manual integration. Reluctance to adopt new technologies due to lack of technical skills or perceived complexity.

pain_signals.evidence_detail: Assumption based on the challenges of manual inventory management. No direct evidence yet.
pain_signals.impact: Money (lost revenue from waste or missed sales). Risk (inaccurate financial reporting). Time (spent manually counting inventory).

pain_signals.description: Reconciling cash and digital payments is time-consuming and prone to errors, especially at the end of a long market day [cite: E4].
pain_signals.evidence_detail: Assumption based on the nature of cash transactions and manual record-keeping.
pain_signals.impact: Time (hours spent reconciling). Risk (inaccurate financial records, potential tax issues).

pain_signals.description: High transaction fees from payment processors (e.g., Square, PayPal) erode profit margins, especially for low-value transactions [cite: E3].
pain_signals.evidence_detail: Standard transaction fees for payment processors range from 2.5% to 3.5% per transaction. [CONFIRMED]

pain_signals.description: Unreliable internet connectivity at some farmers market locations makes it difficult to process digital payments and access cloud-based services [cite: E4].
pain_signals.evidence_detail: Assumption based on the outdoor and often rural locations of farmers markets.
pain_signals.impact: Time (delays in processing payments). Risk (lost sales if unable to accept digital payments). Frustration (for both vendors and customers).

pain_signals.description: Many customers still prefer to pay with cash, creating a barrier to digital payment adoption and increasing the complexity of managing transactions [cite: E4].
pain_signals.evidence_detail: General knowledge about payment preferences. Needs validation with specific data on farmers market customer behavior.
pain_signals.impact: Time (handling cash transactions). Risk (security concerns related to cash).

uncomfortable_insights.insight: Some vendors may prefer the simplicity and perceived control of cash transactions over digital payments, even if it is less efficient [cite: E4].
uncomfortable_insights.implication: Adoption of a digital payment solution may be slower than anticipated. The app needs to offer very compelling benefits to overcome this resistance.

uncomfortable_insights.insight: The target market may have limited technical skills and access to reliable internet, making adoption of a mobile app challenging [cite: E4].
uncomfortable_insights.implication: The app must be extremely user-friendly and work well in offline mode, and training/support must be readily available. This will increase development and support costs.

what_customers_dont_care_about.assumed_need: Advanced analytics and reporting features [cite: E4].
what_customers_dont_care_about.reality: Vendors may prioritize basic sales tracking and inventory management over sophisticated data analysis. They might not have the time or expertise to interpret complex reports.

what_customers_dont_care_about.assumed_need: Integration with complex accounting software [cite: E4].
what_customers_dont_care_about.reality: Many small vendors may use simple bookkeeping methods or outsource accounting tasks. Direct integration might be unnecessary and add unnecessary complexity.

technical_architecture.architecture_style: Hybrid Architecture: Combining elements of Microservices and Monolith. Certain core functionalities like payment processing and user management will be designed as microservices to ensure scalability and resilience. Inventory management and reporting, which are less critical for real-time performance, can initially reside within a monolithic core. This hybrid approach allows for faster initial development (monolith) while still addressing critical scalability concerns (microservices). As the application matures, more functionality can be broken out into microservices.
technical_architecture.architecture_diagram_description: The system comprises a mobile app (iOS and Android) interacting with an API Gateway. The API Gateway routes requests to either the Core Platform (handling inventory, reporting) or dedicated microservices (Payment Processing, User Management). The Core Platform interacts with a primary PostgreSQL database. A Redis cache is used for frequently accessed data (e.g., product details, vendor profiles). Background jobs (e.g., generating reports, syncing offline transactions) are handled by a message queue (RabbitMQ) and worker processes. The system integrates with a Payment Gateway (Stripe or similar) for processing transactions. The mobile app utilizes local storage for offline transaction queuing.

technical_architecture.data_storage: PostgreSQL is the primary data store for all persistent data, including user profiles, product catalog, inventory levels, sales data, and transaction history. Read replicas can be used to scale read operations. Caching with Redis is used for frequently accessed data to improve performance. Data partitioning can be implemented based on vendor ID to improve query performance and scalability. Regular backups are performed to ensure data recovery in case of failure. Data retention policies are defined to comply with legal and regulatory requirements.
technical_architecture.security_architecture: Authentication is handled using Auth0 with OAuth 2.0. Authorization is based on RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), with different roles for vendors, admins, and customers. Data is encrypted at rest using PostgreSQL's encryption features and in transit using HTTPS. API security measures include rate limiting, input validation, and output encoding. Compliance considerations include PCI DSS for payment processing and GDPR for user data privacy.
technical_architecture.scalability_approach: Horizontal scaling is the primary approach for scaling the application. The API Gateway, Core Platform, and Payment Service can be scaled horizontally by adding more instances behind a load balancer. Auto-scaling can be triggered based on CPU utilization or request latency. Database scaling can be achieved using read replicas and data partitioning. Redis is used for caching to reduce database load. A CDN (Content Delivery Network) can be used to serve static assets (images, CSS, JavaScript).
technical_architecture.deployment_strategy: The application is deployed using a containerization approach with Docker. Kubernetes is used for orchestration. The environment structure includes dev, staging, and production environments. Blue-green deployments are used to minimize downtime during deployments. Rollback procedures are defined to quickly revert to a previous version in case of issues.

risk_matrix.name: Competition from Existing POS Systems
risk_matrix.description: Established POS systems (e.g., Square, Shopify) already serve some farmers market vendors. These systems may have features or brand recognition that are difficult to overcome.
triggers: Competitors offering similar features at lower prices.
Negative reviews comparing the app to existing POS systems.
early_warning_signs: High churn rate due to feature gaps.
Competitor feature releases that mirror the app's functionality.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Focus on niche features specific to farmers markets (e.g., offline mode, vendor-specific reporting).

risk_matrix.name: Technical Debt due to Rushed Development
risk_matrix.description: Pressure to launch quickly may lead to shortcuts in development, resulting in bugs, instability, and scalability issues.
early_warning_signs: Difficulty scaling the app to handle more users.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Prioritize code quality and testing, even if it means delaying the initial launch.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Allocate resources to address technical debt and refactor code.

risk_matrix.name: Insufficient Funding
risk_matrix.description: Lack of sufficient capital may limit marketing efforts, slow down development, and hinder the ability to scale the business.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Develop a detailed financial plan and secure sufficient funding before launch.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Reduce expenses, seek bridge financing, or explore alternative revenue streams.

risk_matrix.name: Team Inexperience
risk_matrix.description: Lack of experience in the agriculture/retail industry or mobile app development could lead to poor decisions and execution.
triggers: Inability to effectively market the app.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Hire experienced personnel or consultants to provide guidance.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Restructure the team or outsource certain functions.

risk_matrix.name: Changing Regulations
risk_matrix.description: Changes in regulations related to payments, data privacy, or agriculture could impact the app's functionality or legality.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Stay informed about regulatory changes and adapt the app accordingly.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Consult with legal counsel and make necessary changes to the app.

risk_matrix.name: Security Breach
risk_matrix.description: A security breach could compromise user data, damage the company's reputation, and lead to legal liabilities.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Implement robust security measures, including encryption, firewalls, and intrusion detection systems.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Implement incident response plan, notify affected users, and cooperate with law enforcement.

risk_matrix.name: Offline Transaction Issues
risk_matrix.description: Bugs in the offline transaction queuing and syncing process could result in lost sales or inaccurate records.
early_warning_signs: Data discrepancies between online and offline records.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Thoroughly test the offline transaction functionality and implement robust error handling.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Provide manual reconciliation tools and offer customer support to resolve transaction issues.

risk_matrix.name: Low Adoption Rate
risk_matrix.description: Farmers market vendors may be resistant to adopting new technology or may not see the value proposition of the app.
triggers: Lack of awareness about the app.
High switching costs from existing solutions.
early_warning_signs: Negative feedback about the app's usability.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Conduct user research to understand vendor needs and address their concerns. Offer training and support to help vendors get started.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Refine the app's value proposition and target early adopters.

risk_matrix.name: Supplier Dependency
risk_matrix.description: Reliance on a single payment processor or cloud hosting provider could create vulnerabilities if those suppliers experience outages or increase their prices.
triggers: Changes in supplier terms of service.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Diversify suppliers and negotiate favorable terms.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Switch to alternative suppliers or develop in-house solutions.

risk_matrix.name: Inaccurate Sales Forecasting
risk_matrix.description: Overly optimistic sales forecasts could lead to overspending and cash flow problems.
triggers: Unrealistic assumptions about market size and adoption rate.
risk_matrix.mitigation_strategy: Develop realistic sales forecasts based on market research and historical data. Track key metrics and adjust forecasts as needed.
risk_matrix.contingency_plan: Reduce expenses and seek additional funding.

top_3_risks.name: Insufficient Funding
top_3_risks.why_critical: Lack of funding could cripple the business's ability to grow and compete.
top_3_risks.immediate_action: Secure additional funding through investors or loans.

top_3_risks.name: Technical Debt due to Rushed Development
top_3_risks.why_critical: Technical debt can lead to instability and make it difficult to add new features.
top_3_risks.immediate_action: Allocate developer time to refactor code and address bugs.

top_3_risks.name: Competition from Existing POS Systems
top_3_risks.why_critical: Strong competition can limit market share and revenue potential.
top_3_risks.immediate_action: Differentiate the app with unique features and targeted marketing.

conditions_for_go: Thorough testing of offline transaction functionality.

key_risk_indicators.threshold: Below 5% growth MoM for 3 consecutive months
key_risk_indicators.action_if_exceeded: Re-evaluate marketing strategy and product features.
Conduct churn analysis to identify root causes and implement retention strategies.
Investigate and fix bugs in the offline transaction syncing process.

monitoring_plan.escalation_process: Risks exceeding thresholds are immediately escalated to the executive team for review and action.

prototype.story_summary: The prototype shows Maria Rodriguez, a farm stand owner, receiving a low-stock alert on her dashboard for a best-selling product. She drills into her inventory, confirms the low stock, and then proactively adds a new seasonal product to the system in just a few clicks. The 'aha moment' is the speed and ease with which she can manage her inventory digitally, saving her time and preparing her for a successful market day.

Micro-interactions like hover states and smooth transitions create a polished, high-fidelity user experience.

views.tailored_summary:
This initiative presents a dual-stream revenue model targeting the underserved farmers market vendor segment. Revenue is generated through a tiered SaaS subscription and a competitive transaction fee on payments, projected to contribute 40% and 60% respectively. The model is benchmarked against established competitors like Square, aiming for a competitive advantage through lower processing fees and niche features.

The initial financial outlay is focused on personnel for a lean development team and operational costs, with a clear path to scaling. The financial model projects reaching approximately $1.2M in annual revenue by Year 3, contingent on achieving user adoption targets. The most significant financial risks identified are market competition from incumbents and the accuracy of our customer acquisition cost (CAC) and adoption rate assumptions, which are currently based on industry data and hypotheses.
key_questions_answered: What are the primary revenue streams and their estimated contribution?
What is the projected cost structure for the first two years?
What is the pricing model and how does it compare to key competitors?
What are the key financial assumptions underpinning the revenue projections?
What is the estimated Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) for primary channels?

anticipated_objections.objection: The revenue projections seem optimistic and are based on unverified assumptions.
anticipated_objections.response: This is a valid concern. The projections are based on hypotheses that require validation. The Go-to-Market plan includes a phased rollout in a beachhead market specifically to test pricing sensitivity, adoption rates, and transaction volume to create a data-driven forecast before scaling investment.

anticipated_objections.objection: The Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) of $30-$100 seems low for a new market entrant.
anticipated_objections.response: The estimated CAC is an initial benchmark. Our channel strategy prioritizes cost-effective methods like content marketing and direct sales at markets, where we can acquire multiple vendors at once. We will be tracking this metric rigorously from day one to validate and adjust our channel mix.

anticipated_objections.objection: The compliance costs for PCI DSS seem high and could impact our timeline and budget.
anticipated_objections.response: The cost is a necessary investment to operate in this space and mitigate significant financial and reputational risk. We plan to manage this by integrating with a certified third-party payment processor initially, which significantly reduces our PCI DSS scope and upfront cost, allowing us to enter the market faster while we work towards full compliance.

views.decision_recommendation: Recommend conditional approval for a seed funding round focused on a 6-month validation phase. This phase should aim to convert key E4/E5 assumptions in the financial model to E2/E3 evidence before committing to a full-scale development budget.

views.tailored_summary:
This briefing confirms that payment processing is a core function of the proposed product, making security and compliance paramount from day one. We have identified PCI DSS as the primary regulatory requirement, which carries a high impact level. The plan acknowledges the significant effort required, estimating a 6-12 month timeline and a budget of $10-50k for initial compliance activities.

The technical architecture proposes mitigating risk by leveraging a certified third-party payment processor, which will offload a significant portion of our compliance burden initially. Security is factored into the technology stack, with plans for data encryption in transit and at rest. The primary risks from a security perspective are ensuring end-to-end data protection for cardholder data and managing the compliance overhead. We have a foundational plan to address these risks, but it requires further detailed scoping.
key_questions_answered: What are the primary regulatory and compliance obligations?
How will the system handle and protect sensitive cardholder data?
What is the estimated cost and timeline for achieving PCI DSS compliance?
What security risks have been identified and what are the mitigation strategies?
How does the technical architecture address security concerns?

anticipated_objections.objection: The plan to achieve PCI DSS compliance in 6-12 months seems aggressive for a new team.
anticipated_objections.response: The timeline is ambitious but achievable because our strategy is to initially limit our scope by integrating with a fully compliant payment gateway like Stripe. This transfers much of the burden, allowing us to focus on securing our application and processes. We will not be building our own payment vault in the initial phase.

anticipated_objections.objection: The $10k-$50k compliance cost estimate is too vague. This could spiral.
anticipated_objections.response: This is a preliminary estimate. To refine this, our immediate next step should be to engage a Qualified Security Assessor (QSA) for a formal scoping exercise. This will provide a more precise budget and a detailed roadmap for compliance, which we can execute against.

anticipated_objections.objection: Data privacy beyond PCI DSS, like state-level laws, is mentioned but not detailed.
anticipated_objections.response: Correct. We've identified State Data Breach Notification Laws as applicable. A full Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) will be part of our next phase to detail requirements for PII handling, storage, user consent, and breach notification procedures for all relevant jurisdictions.

views.decision_recommendation: Recommend approval to proceed, with the mandatory requirement that a security-focused discovery phase is funded. This phase must produce a detailed compliance roadmap, a data flow architecture, and a refined budget for security and compliance activities before development begins.

views.tailored_summary:
The proposed technical solution is a hybrid architecture, balancing the development speed of a monolith for non-critical features with the scalability and resilience of microservices for core functions like payment processing and user management. This pragmatic approach allows for rapid initial delivery while de-risking the most critical, high-throughput components of the system from the outset. The plan includes a clear path for evolving the architecture by breaking out further microservices as the product matures.

The technology stack is centered on React Native for cross-platform mobile development, enabling a single codebase for both iOS and Android to maximize development efficiency. The backend stack leverages proven, scalable technologies. Key technical challenges, such as the need for robust offline functionality for use in environments with poor connectivity, have been identified as a critical product requirement and will influence the data synchronization and storage architecture.
key_questions_answered: What is the proposed architectural style and the rationale behind it?
What is the core technology stack and why were these technologies chosen?
How does the architecture plan to handle scalability for core functions like payments?
How will the system support critical features like offline mode?
What are the alternatives considered for the key technology choices?

anticipated_objections.objection: A hybrid architecture can introduce complexity in deployment and testing. Why not a pure monolith to start?
anticipated_objections.response: While a pure monolith is simpler initially, it introduces significant risk around our most critical component: payments. By isolating payments as a microservice, we gain scalability, independent deployment, and a contained scope for PCI DSS compliance, which is a significant architectural advantage. This is a strategic trade-off of minor initial complexity for major long-term risk reduction.

anticipated_objections.objection: React Native has known performance limitations compared to native development.
anticipated_objections.response: This is a valid consideration. However, for our application's primary use cases—forms, lists, and transaction processing—React Native's performance is more than adequate. This choice allows us to reach both iOS and Android markets with a smaller team and faster iteration cycles, which is critical at this early stage. We will conduct performance profiling on key user flows.

anticipated_objections.objection: The plan for data persistence and offline synchronization is not detailed.
anticipated_objections.response: Correct, this is a high-level plan. Offline functionality is a complex requirement and a key differentiator. A dedicated technical spike and proof-of-concept are required in the next phase to determine the optimal strategy for local data storage, conflict resolution, and synchronization logic before we commit to a specific implementation.

views.decision_recommendation: Recommend approval of the high-level architecture and technology stack. Mandate that the initial development phase begins with technical spikes and PoCs for the payment integration and offline functionality before full feature development commences.

views.tailored_summary:
This initiative targets a clear market need among farmers market vendors, focusing on pain points that general-purpose POS systems like Square do not adequately address. Our primary persona, 'Maria Rodriguez', encapsulates the frustrations of manual inventory tracking, payment reconciliation, and lost sales—problems our core product epics like 'Inventory Management' and 'Sales & Reporting' are designed to solve directly. The evidence for these pain points is currently hypothetical and requires validation, which is a top priority.

Our competitive strategy is not to beat Square on all fronts, but to win in a specific niche by being the best purpose-built tool for our target customer. Differentiation will come from features tailored to their unique workflow, such as robust offline functionality, management of perishable goods, and vendor-centric analytics. The Go-to-Market strategy focuses on a direct, high-touch approach in a specific beachhead market, allowing us to validate our core hypotheses and build a loyal user base before expanding.
key_questions_answered: Who is the target customer and what are their primary pain points?
How does our product solve these problems better than existing competitors like Square?
What is the core value proposition and our key market differentiator?
What is the go-to-market strategy for acquiring our first 100 customers?
What are the critical features for the Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?

anticipated_objections.objection: The entire product is based on E4-level hypotheses about user pain. We don't have proof customers want this.
anticipated_objections.response: This is the most critical risk, and the plan is designed to address it head-on. The 'Top Validation Priorities' explicitly call this out. The next step is not to build the full product, but to conduct intensive customer discovery interviews and prototype testing with vendors in our beachhead market to validate these hypotheses before a single line of production code is written.

anticipated_objections.objection: Square has a free product and massive brand recognition. How can we possibly compete?
anticipated_objections.response: We compete by being specific. Square is a generic tool; we are a specialized instrument. Our free tier allows us to achieve parity for entry-level users, but our paid tiers will offer features Square is unlikely to build, such as tracking inventory by harvest date or analytics comparing sales across different markets. Our GTM targets vendors already using Square, indicating they are open to digital tools but may be underserved.

anticipated_objections.objection: The product roadmap seems too ambitious. 'Inventory Management' alone is a huge epic.
anticipated_objections.response: The epics represent the long-term vision. The MVP will be a thin slice through the most critical user stories, such as 'Add New Product' and 'Process a Sale'. We will ruthlessly prioritize the 'jobs-to-be-done' for our persona to launch with a minimal but highly valuable feature set that solves their most pressing problem first.

views.decision_recommendation: Strongly recommend funding a 3-month 'Product Discovery & Validation' phase. The goal is to convert our E4 hypotheses into E2 verified evidence. Defer a decision on funding full MVP development until the results of this validation phase are presented.

common_concerns: The business case and product strategy rely heavily on unvalidated E4 (Hypothesis) and E5 (Assumption) level evidence, particularly concerning customer pain points and financial projections.
The timeline and cost for achieving mandatory PCI DSS compliance represent a significant hurdle that could impact both budget and time-to-market.
Competition from established, well-funded players like Square POS is a major market risk that requires a clear and sustainable differentiation strategy.
alignment_opportunities: All stakeholders can align on the immediate need for a funded 'Validation Phase' to convert assumptions into evidence before committing to larger-scale investment.

There is a shared understanding that leveraging a third-party payment processor is the most pragmatic approach to de-risk and accelerate initial market entry from a financial, security, and technical perspective.

experiments.target_profile: Farmers market vendors who have been selling for at least 2 seasons and currently use a mix of cash, digital payment apps (like Venmo/Square), and/or pen and paper for tracking.
experiments.specific_instructions: 1. Prepare a semi-structured interview script focused on current processes. 2. Ask open-ended questions about how they track sales, manage inventory, and handle payments. 3. Probe for specific pain points, time spent on administrative tasks, and costs of current tools. 4. Use the '5 Whys' technique to understand the root cause of frustrations. 5. Only briefly mention the app concept at the end to gauge initial reaction, without selling.
experiments.success_criteria: At least 7 out of 10 vendors explicitly state significant frustration with their current process and identify a specific, recurring pain point related to inventory, sales tracking, or payment reconciliation.
experiments.failure_criteria: Fewer than 3 out of 10 vendors can identify a significant pain point, or the majority state their current 'good enough' solution works fine.
experiments.risk_if_skipped: Building a solution for a problem that doesn't exist or isn't painful enough for vendors to pay to solve, leading to low adoption and failure. Directly addresses RISK-001.

experiments.target_profile: Farmers market vendors in online communities (e.g., Facebook Groups for makers and farmers, Reddit's r/farmersmarket).
experiments.specific_instructions: 1. Create a 5-minute online survey. 2. Briefly present the value proposition (e.g., 'Save 3 hours a week, track inventory easily, accept any payment'). 3. List the features for the 'Basic' ($9.99/mo) and 'Pro' ($29.99/mo) tiers. 4. Use a Van Westendorp pricing sensitivity analysis, asking at what price the 'Basic' plan would be 'Too cheap,' 'A bargain,' 'Getting expensive,' and 'Too expensive.' 5. Ask a final question: 'Based on the features, which tier would you choose?'
experiments.success_criteria: The optimal price point derived from the survey for the Basic tier is between $8 and $15. At least 30% of respondents indicate they would select the Basic or Pro tier at the proposed prices.
experiments.failure_criteria: The optimal price point is below $5, or fewer than 10% of respondents indicate they would pay for a subscription.
experiments.risk_if_skipped: Mispricing the product, leading to either low revenue due to underpricing or low adoption due to overpricing. The entire financial model (BC-8) would be invalid.

experiments.target_profile: Individuals with interests in 'farmers markets,' 'small business ownership,' 'artisan goods,' and 'local farming' on social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram.
experiments.specific_instructions: 1. Build a simple landing page using a tool like Carrd or Webflow. 2. The page must have a clear headline (e.g., 'The Easiest Way to Run Your Market Stall'), 3 key benefits with icons, and a single call-to-action (CTA). 3. The CTA button will say 'Get Early Access'. 4. Clicking the CTA leads to a simple form asking for an email address. 5. After submission, a thank you page explains the product is still in development. 6. Run A/B tests on ad copy and headlines. Track cost per click (CPC) and cost per email signup (CPA).
experiments.success_criteria: Achieve a cost per email acquisition (CPA) of $15 or less. Achieve a landing page conversion rate of over 5%.

experiments.target_profile: 5-8 vendors from the initial interviews (EXP-1) who expressed high interest and are not highly tech-savvy.
experiments.specific_instructions: 1. Create a clickable, non-functional prototype in Figma or a similar tool. 2. The prototype should only cover the 3 core tasks: adding an inventory item, processing a cash sale, and viewing the daily sales total. 3. Sit with the vendor and ask them to perform these 3 tasks on a mobile device while thinking aloud. 4. Do not provide any guidance unless they are completely stuck. 5. Record task completion success/failure, time on task, and qualitative feedback.
experiments.success_criteria: At least 80% of testers can complete all 3 core tasks successfully without any help. The average user rating for ease-of-use (on a 1-5 scale) is 4.0 or higher.
experiments.failure_criteria: More than 50% of testers fail to complete one or more core tasks, or the workflow is consistently described as 'confusing' or 'difficult'.
experiments.risk_if_skipped: Building an app that is difficult to use, leading to high churn, poor reviews, and an inability to compete with established players (RISK-001). Wasted development resources (RISK-002).

experiments.target_profile: 2-3 farmers market vendors who are willing to let you shadow them for a full market day.
experiments.specific_instructions: 1. Act as the human backend for the app. Use a spreadsheet on a tablet to track their inventory in real-time. 2. Use your personal Square/Stripe reader to accept card payments for them. 3. At the end of the day, immediately provide them with a detailed sales report you generate manually. 4. After the report, present the pricing plans ($9.99/$29.99) and ask, 'Based on the service today, would you be willing to pay for this?' and attempt to collect payment for the first month.
experiments.success_criteria: At least 2 of the 3 vendors agree to pay for the first month of service after the concierge test is complete. This provides the strongest possible evidence for the revenue model.
experiments.failure_criteria: None of the vendors are willing to pay, indicating a major gap between perceived value and actual value.
experiments.cost_estimate: $100 for expenses (e.g., data plan, lunch for vendor)
experiments.risk_if_skipped: Grossly overestimating revenue projections (BC-8) by failing to test if users will actually convert from expressing interest to becoming paying customers.
